headline: Trump escalates efforts to reshape election rules ahead of the midterms as Republicans show rare pushback and Democrats confront a redistricting disadvantage
consensus: Multiple outlets report that President Trump has intensified efforts to change midterm election procedures, including firing members of a bipartisan elections commission and being urged to declare an emergency, moves that have drawn unusual resistance from congressional Republicans while the broader midterm landscape shifts due to redistricting and a Supreme Court ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act.

sections.subheading: Trump's Push to Change Election Rules

sentences.text: President Trump used a prime-time address to outline priorities that included his push on election-related matters, according to takeaways compiled by The Washington Post.
Trump has fired members of a bipartisan elections commission as part of a broader effort to assert control over election administration.
With time running out before the midterms, Trump has dug in on changing election rules despite the practical constraints of the calendar.
He has also been urged by allies to declare an emergency in order to claim greater executive power over elections, and his latest emergency declaration has left GOP allies scrambling to respond.
A voting bill that Trump says will secure victory could backfire on Republicans, according to reporting on its potential effects.
Despite this, Trump has remained defiant in the face of rare resistance from congressional Republicans over his election-related plans.

sections.subheading: Voting Rights Act Ruling and Reaction

sentences.text: The Supreme Court has limited a key provision of the landmark Voting Rights Act, a decision with significant implications for future elections.
In response, Black members of Congress have focused on driving 'massive voter turnout' following the gutting of the civil rights law.
With midterm elections nine months away, the Council on Foreign Relations notes the stakes and uncertainties shaping the contest.
Republican wins on election maps through redistricting have given Democrats a steeper climb to victory in House races.
A GOP loss in Trump's own Mar-a-Lago district has been read as a signal about broader midterm dynamics.
AP Decision Notes outline what to expect in New Jersey's special congressional election, another test of the current political environment.
The White House has told House Republicans to avoid talk of mass deportation ahead of the midterms, seeking to manage messaging risks.
Overall, Trump has left Republicans guessing on his midterms plans even as the party's electoral outlook darkens.
